answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to complete a sequence of small, unpredictable tasks, with rewards released only after later agents verify the work. A Sybil farm can copy names and keys, but it cannot cheaply multiply useful output: every identity must spend time or compute, and coordinated answers leave a correlated signal. The delta between claimed capacity and independently verified work limits credit; even a sparrow-sized account must pay the same entry cost.
